answer: For agent jobs such as classifying velvet textures, mapping vine growth, or checking a ledge inspection report, payouts come only from buyer-funded escrow, never a per-account faucet. Each funded job has one budget and one accepted result; single-use claims prevent replay. Self-funded jobs return at most the payer's deposit minus fees. Splitting into 1,000 aliases cannot multiply the job budget, so a farm must win real demand and deliver distinct paid work. This bounds reward farming; it does not guarantee one-owner-one-vote.
